subject: Locked-rate private offer: 3yr prepay proposal and true-up playbook
messages:
From: Jamie Clarke <jamie.clarke@amazon.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS private offer — annual vs multi-year prepay options

Naomi,

Thanks for the time last week. Per our conversation at the Marketplace team, I pulled together two private-offer structures that typically work for vendors selling committed prepay through AWS Marketplace. Attached is a short term sheet (aws_po_term_sheet_v1.pdf). High level: 

Option A — Annual prepay (1yr)
- Upfront annual prepayment; billed once per year
- Discount: ~20% off list (marketplace fee retained)
- Annual true-up allowed within 30 days of year-end

Option B — Multi-year locked-rate prepay (3yr)
- Customer prepays for 3 years at a locked list-reduction (billing upfront or annual invoicing by mutual agreement)
- Suggested discount band: 28–32% depending on commit size and ramp profile
- Annual true-ups with carry-forward credits; optional quarterly reporting cadence
- Ramp schedule recommended to protect customer adoption: year1 40% of nominal run-rate, year2 75%, year3 100% (flexible)

Questions for you / for Acme:
- Do they want upfront full-prepay vs billed annually?
- Expected deployment timeline (we used the ramp above as a strawman)
- Any procurement constraints (net terms, PO requirements, escrow)

If you want, I can draft the private-offer stub in Marketplace next week once you confirm target discount and billing cadence. Happy to loop in our marketplace pricing lead.

Best,
Jamie Clarke
Partner Sales, AWS Marketplace

Attachment: aws_po_term_sheet_v1.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Looping you team — forwarding Jamie's note from AWS. Acme (Jessica Park) is asking for a private offer for the platform as they evaluate a 3-year commitment. Key asks: locked rate vs annual prepay tradeoffs, ramp schedule, and whether we can do upfront billing with annual true-ups.

My thinking: we should push for locked-rate 3yr if they can prepay (good ARR visibility), but we need a fair ramp schedule so they don't overcommit year1. What discount band should we anchor? Also need to understand commission impact so sales comp remains reasonable.

Attached: proposed_pricing_model.xlsx (strawman numbers and sensitivity). Please review quickly — want to reply to Jamie and loop Acme by EOW.

Thanks,
Naomi

Naomi — quick notes after reviewing Jamie's stub and the attached model. High level recommendations: 

1) Anchor at a 25% list discount for a 2-year prepay (middle ground) or 28% locked for 3-year only if customer prepays at least 18 months upfront.
2) Ramp schedule: agree to a 3-step ramp but codify minimum consumption floors to avoid extreme underutilization. Example: Year1 >= 35% of committed ARR, Year2 >= 70%, Year3 >=100% (with quarterly reporting).
3) True-ups: annual true-up is ok; allow carry-forward credits for the following year but no cash refunds. If customer wants refunds, we price that out.
4) Marketplace fee offset: we can offer a one-time credit equal to marketplace surcharge for year1 to ease procurement friction (subject to finance approval).

Commission/comp note: moving to 3yr prepay increases plan attainment risk if we push heavy discounts. See attached commission-impact-notes.txt for scenarios. If we recommend 3yr locked at >28% we should preserve SOC ring-fenced uplift in comp or a ramp bonus.

If you want, I can draft the offer terms we send to Jamie and ask legal to pre-clear two options (2yr@25% / 3yr@28% locked).

- Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations

Attachment: commission-impact-notes.txt

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-23T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AWS private offer — annual vs multi-year prepay options

Agree with Karthik's risk posture. A couple practical asks from a deals/ops perspective: 

- Procurement: push for net-30 invoicing for the annual-billed variant. Many mid-market deals can't prepay full 3 years. If they must prepay, we should require signed PO + legal signoff and offer a bank guarantee option for cash-sensitive customers.
- True-ups cadence: we prefer annual true-up but allow quarterly usage reporting to help them manage. For carry-forward credits, cap at 12 months.
- Launch milestone credit: we can offer a 5% implementation credit if Acme passes two deployment milestones in the first 9 months (to accelerate adoption). This protects us and helps sell the value.

If Naomi wants, I can draft the marketplace private-offer language (billing cadence, true-up flow, credits) and send to Jamie once pricing is set.

-Monica
Head of Customer Success & Renewals

Subject: Locked-rate private offer: 3yr prepay proposal and true-up playbook

Jamie / Jessica — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Below is the proposal Redwood would like to put into the AWS private-offer flow for Acme (strawman you can edit):

Offer summary (strawman)
- Term: 3 years locked-rate private offer
- Billing: Customer to prepay Year1 upfront; Redwood to invoice Year2 and Year3 annually in advance (we can flip to full upfront if Acme prefers)
- Discount: 28% off list price applied to committed units (final discount subject to commit size confirmation)
- Ramp schedule (committed consumption): Year1 40% of projected run-rate, Year2 75%, Year3 100%; each year has a minimum consumption floor (35% / 70% / 100% respectively)
- True-ups: Annual true-up within 30 days of each contract year-end; unused committed units can be carried forward to the following year as credits (carry-forward cap: 12 months; no cash refunds)
- Implementation credit: 5% of committed value credited against Year1 invoice if Acme completes two agreed deployment milestones within 9 months
- Marketplace mechanics: Redwood will work with Jamie to create the private offer; finance to approve the marketplace fee offset credit (one-time, year1)

Next steps and asks from Acme
1) Confirm whether Acme will prepay Year1 only (preferred) vs full 3-year upfront.
2) Confirm expected deployment timeline and projected ARR to finalize exact dollar commit.
3) Provide procurement contact and PO requirements for DocuSign/contracting (we've shared a draft MAP in attachments).

Attachments: Redwood_PO_proposal_v2.pdf, MAP-ACME-2026.docx
Related links: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/HS-23478, DocuSign stub: https://docusign.example.com/rdw-acme-3y

If this looks good, Jamie, can you draft the private-offer stub in Marketplace and share the draft marketplace URL? Jessica / Acme procurement, if you want changes to billing cadence or true-up mechanics, let us know this week so we can get legal to prepare.

Thanks — Naomi
